_note: Road to The Crown story beats, one per stage (six stages). Original characters and places. Illustrated panels arrive with final art.
kofi: Accra taught you to fly; South London cages taught you to land. Tonight a market lane hangs a hoop on a heritage arch, and the rain says nobody dunks here. Prove the rain wrong.
Under the elevated line the fence shakes every forty seconds. The locals say you only float because nobody has bodied you yet. Get bodied. Float anyway.
A packed gym that remembers every name on its banners. They chant for the home kid. Give them a new one to chant.
Golden hour on the quad. A scout in a scarf watches from the grass, pen still. Make it move.
The Old Barn smells like a hundred years of finals. The organist plays you in like you belong. Do you?
The Crown. One spotlight, one rim, one last takeoff from the line. Gravity has been patient with you long enough.
meera: You learned on monsoon-wet concrete, where the ball skids and only a true release survives. The bazaar is your kind of floor.
The DJ at the Tracks cuts the music when you rise. The whole block counts it down with you. Make the splash louder than the train.
A student section paints your number on their faces to mock you. By the second half, they are counting your stacks.
Leaves drift through the quad like confetti nobody ordered. Rhythm, not hurry. One, two, three.
Old wooden rims, older stories. They say nobody shoots from that far in the Barn. Nobody had your feet.
Finals at The Crown. The jumbotron is waiting for your last release. Let it rain.
juno: The clip that went viral was filmed in slow motion. Tonight there is no slow motion, only a market crowd and a defender who has watched your tape.
The Tracks crowd presses against the chain-link to see your handles up close. Give them a frame they cannot pause.
Rivalry Night. The biggest kid in the county is guarding you. Bigs block small guards at the rim. So do not go to the rim. Go through his ankles.
On the quad, everyone has a phone up. Perfect. Lag them.
In the Barn, the floorboards creak with every crossover. Make the building flinch.
The Crown's glass and spotlights were made for light trails. Overclock the whole arena.
matas: From the Baltic coast to a monsoon bazaar. You do not talk much. The post bumps talk for you.
Under the Tracks, they say the train is the only thing that moves you. Lean on them until they believe it.
A school gym full of shooters who think you are too slow. You are. You are also standing where they need to go.
The quad's maple leaves crunch under every drop-step. Somewhere a band is rehearsing. Give them a drum beat.
The Old Barn's rim has hung for eighty years. Hang on it a little longer.
The Crown. Three bumps, a crack in the floor, a two-hand hammer. Make the foundations remember you.
